title: Azure Key Vault Overview
description: Learn what Azure Key Vault does, why you should centralize secrets, and how it protects cryptographic keys.

data.text: Azure Key Vault is a cloud service for securely storing and accessing secrets. A secret can be a password, API key, certificate, or cryptographic key. Key Vault keeps these items encrypted and controls who can access them.
Key Vault also provides hardware security module (HSM) backed keys for scenarios that require FIPS 140-2 compliance.

data.title: Key Vault Objects
items: Secrets — passwords, connection strings, API keys
Keys — RSA or elliptic-curve keys for encryption and signing
Certificates — TLS/SSL or code-signing certificates with auto-renewal

rows: Key Vault SDK or REST API

data.title: Create a Key Vault with Azure CLI
data.content: Provision a new Key Vault in your resource group.
data.code: az keyvault create   --name myKeyVault   --resource-group myResourceGroup   --location eastus   --enable-soft-delete true

data.title: Soft Delete
data.text: Always enable soft-delete on Key Vault. If someone accidentally deletes a secret, soft-delete lets you recover it within the retention period.

Key Vault is a managed service, but it is not a single global service. Each vault lives in a region and has its own DNS name, firewall, and access model. That matters for latency, disaster recovery, and private networking. Secrets are encrypted at rest with keys managed by Microsoft by default; for stricter requirements you can use a customer-managed key in a Managed HSM.

data.title: Create a production-ready vault
data.content: Enable soft-delete and purge protection so that a deleted vault or secret can be recovered, and enable RBAC authorization so access is managed with normal role assignments.
data.code:
az keyvault create \
  --name shop-kv \
  --resource-group rg-shop \
  --location eastus \
  --enable-soft-delete true \
  --retention-days 90 \
  --enable-purge-protection true \
  --enable-rbac-authorization true

az keyvault secret set --vault-name shop-kv --name SqlPassword --value "S3cure!"
az keyvault secret show --vault-name shop-kv --name SqlPassword --query value -o tsv

data.text: Vault tiers and when to use them

rows: Most application secrets and TLS certificates
HSM-backed keys for all key types
Regulated workloads that require hardware key protection
High-assurance key operations and strict separation of duties

data.title: Soft-delete changes the meaning of delete
data.text: Deleting a secret or vault moves it to a recoverable state for the retention period. With purge protection enabled, even an administrator cannot permanently delete it early. This protects against ransomware inside your own subscription, but it also means test cleanup needs a purge step.

data.title: What interviewers look for
data.text: Know the three object types, the two permission models, and the recovery features. A strong answer explains why secrets belong in Key Vault rather than app settings: central audit, access control, rotation, and no secret in a deployment artifact or container image.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Key Vault stores secrets, keys, and certificates in one place.
Access is controlled by Entra ID identities and RBAC or access policies.
Soft-delete protects against accidental or malicious deletion.
data.takeaway: Move every hardcoded secret out of your code and into Key Vault.
